subject: Climate & Environment
title: Fog Catchers and Dew Harvesters
description: A 60-second lesson on Fog Catchers and Dew Harvesters.

hook.text: In the Atacama Desert — the driest place on Earth — villages harvest water from fog.

buildup.text: Large mesh nets catch tiny fog droplets, which drip into collection tanks below.

discovery.text: A single fog catcher can collect 200 to 1,000 liters per day depending on conditions.

twist.text: Dew harvesters use radiative cooling to condense moisture from clear night air.

climax.text: These low-tech solutions cost almost nothing to maintain and need no energy at all.

punchline.text: Where there's fog, there's water. You just need a net to catch it.

quiz.question: How do fog catchers collect water?

details.summary: Fog catchers use fine mesh nets to capture water droplets from fog and channel them into collection tanks. Dew harvesters use surfaces that cool overnight to condense atmospheric moisture. These low-tech solutions provide water in arid coastal and mountain communities where other sources are scarce.
details.whyItMatters: Fog and dew harvesting offer simple, low-cost water solutions for some of the world's driest communities. They demonstrate that creative engineering can address scarcity without expensive infrastructure.
takeaways: Mesh nets capture fog droplets in coastal and mountain areas
Dew harvesting condenses atmospheric moisture on cool surfaces
These methods provide water where conventional sources fail

faq.question: How much water can a fog catcher produce?
faq.answer: A standard 40-square-meter fog catcher can harvest 200 to 400 liters per day in favorable conditions. In total, fog collection projects in Chile, Morocco, and Peru supply drinking water to thousands of people in dry coastal and highland communities.

faq.question: Where do fog catchers work best?
faq.answer: Fog catchers work best in areas with frequent, dense fog and consistent wind to push droplets into the mesh. Coastal hills and mountain ridges in the Atacama Desert, the Canary Islands, southern Morocco, and parts of East Africa are ideal locations.
